title: Module 3 Vocabulary Check
intro: Answer each item. Feedback comes right away. Items you miss come back for a retry round.

items.q: Why does the sample variance divide SS by n minus 1 instead of n?
o: Dividing by n would underestimate the population variance on average
Samples are always smaller than populations
It makes the answer an integer
items.why: A sample is centered on its own mean, which makes deviations smaller than they would be from the true mean. Dividing by n minus 1 corrects that bias.

items.q: Degrees of freedom for a single sample variance equal
items.why: Once the sample mean is fixed, only n minus 1 scores are free to vary.

o: Averages out to the population value across many samples
Is computed from the whole population
items.why: Unbiased does not mean any single estimate is correct. It means the long run average is right.

The spread of a single variable

items.q: The sum of products (SP) in the correlation formula
o: Adds up, for each person, the X deviation times the Y deviation
Is the sum of squared X deviations
items.why: SP captures how X and Y deviate together. Positive products dominate when high X goes with high Y.

items.q: The coefficient of determination r squared is
o: The proportion of variability in one variable accounted for by its linear relationship with the other
The probability the correlation is real
items.why: If r = .50, then r squared = .25, so 25 percent of the variability is shared.

o: As one variable increases the other tends to decrease
One variable causes the other to fall
items.why: The sign gives direction. The magnitude gives strength.
Strength depends on the absolute value, not the sign.
